questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Interesting city - relatively close to my home where i have a girlfriend, so she could visit often. Also Freie is known to be a good university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A great expericence but you have to be ready for a lot of administrative work as well. I feel privileged to be able to go, but sometimes you can't help but feel 'there simply has to be a smarter way to do this'.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was ok, but only because of the the Erasmus Student Assistants at the Otto Suhr Institute. They were very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were orientation days for all Erasmus students and a tour of the campus especially for the politcal science students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: (Name of staff removed) were great, and answered all my questions. However the FU did not really give that much info about their pretty complicated course registration process. Luckily (name of staff removed) could answer my questions

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I made a post in a facebook group called 'Danskere i Berlin' for danish people in Berlin. My new roommates offered me a room in their apartment the same day.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That they should do it. If you go to Berlin to study - i would recommend actually living in Berlin to experience the city and not in the suburb of Dahlem where the university is located.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't look that much into it. I was not interested in living on campus of outside of Berlin

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is long time ago now, but i remember it being a bit confusing. Luckily i know a lot of other people who have gone abroad before, so i could ask them.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Confusing and quite stressful - MANY many emails with different deadlines and portals you should log on to.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Other students from my home university who had done it before. And the possibility of writing email to the very helpful student assistants.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to get the exact classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pay CLOSE attention to all the different deadlines in the MANY emails you receive. And people from your home university who have done it before, when in doubt.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall a good experience

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was quite high. There were phd students attending some of my classes, which rasied the level i guess.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The seminars of FU are less 'lectury' than classes at KU. Being able to pass a course with active participation (for fewer points) makes a big difference. The lecturers are for better and worse 'teaching less' in Berlin.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Machine Learning in Social Scienses
Elections in the US
Intermediate Data analysis and Visualization in R
Politics of Trade

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I learned a lot in all of my courses. Depends on people's interests

questions.answer: Had to buy a bed. And i rented a bike.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport is cheap with the semester ticket. Generally berlin is a bit cheaper than cph

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really engage in it, but there were many events and opportunities to meet other international students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Loads of different events. I really dont a have any overview.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Didn't really go to any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Neukölln

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Okay

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: language barrier

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: more diverse and free spirited city - people are less alike. Sometimes in copenhagen, it feels like we are all living the same life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't live in Dahlem - try to find a place in the city. 
You can do courses in other institutes. Some of them are worth more points than at OSI. I did 4 

two at OSI worth 7 and 3 respectively 
two at sociology worth 10 each.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: See last answer.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living abroad - experiencing another city and culture and fall in love with my local neighbourhood. Meeting new people and having a good time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: More time alone that i was used to in the beginning. But everyone will feel different about that.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
